Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Onboarding & Nominations of Key Officials
under e-HRMS 2.0
The Government of India has launched e-HRMS 2.0 to provide end-to-end online HR
services to government employees, including leave, reimbursement, training, and related
modules. This SOP outlines the process for onboarding employees and nominating key
officials for designated roles.
1. Information Required from MDOs
List of Current Places of Postings along with Nomination letters of respective Nodal officers
/ MDO Admin / CCA Admin / AVD Admin
Each Ministry/Department/Organization (MDO) must provide the following details:
List of Current Places of Postings along with Nomination letters of respective
Nodal officers/MDO Admin/CCA Admin/AVD Admin
In-position Strength
Details of Employees
2. Onboarding Process
Step-1: Initiate a formal email request from their respective
Divisions/Departments/Organisations with a point of contact.(Required Info: Name, Mobile
Number, Government email address)
Step-2: In the same email request, the respective division/department has to provide us
with the Following details,
Current Place of Posting
In-position Strength
Step-3: We will verify the hierarchy and functionality based on your requirements.
Step-4: If Criteria falls under the e-HRMS 2.0 requirement, we will initiate a demonstration
session as per your requirement. (Optional)
Step-5: We will ask for the employee’s data as per the template attached from
support.ehrms dopt@gov.in.
 
Instructions to be followed while filling in the employee details,
Fill mandatory fields: Employee Name (without any Mr/Mrs/Shri Salutation),
Father’s Name(without any Mr/Mrs/Shri Salutation), DOB (dd-mm-yyyy),
Designation, Official Email ID (employee-based mail id registered with NIC
eparichay), and 10-digit Mobile Number(without code).
Complete the template for all employees under your
Ministry/Department/Organisation.
Step-6: Also, we use standard template to get the onboarding employee details of
respective Ministry/Department/Organisation.
Step-7: E-HRMS 2.0 Team will onboard employees based on the submitted data and share
confirmation.
Step-8: Employees must complete their profiles 100% on the e-HRMS 2.0 portal after
onboarding.
Step-9: Once completed, employees can start using modules such as Employee
Services(Leaves, Reimbursement, etc.), Financial Records (PaySlips, GPF
Statements), APAR, Property(IPR, Declaration of Finance statements, etc.).
Note: Ensure strict adherence to the prescribed format and fields in the template.
3. Appointment of Nodal Officer
Submit a supporting letter from the Competent Authority endorsing the officer’s role.
The officer should belong to the Administration/Establishment and be closely
monitoring Service Books.
Provide the following details:
Required Detail Description
Name of Officer Nodal officer nominated by competent authority
Designation Official Designation
Date of Birth Officer DOB
Father's Name Without salutation
 
Official Email gov.in / nic.in email ID
Mobile Number 10 digit number
MDO Name Ministry/Department/Organization
Place of Posting Office location
Employees under Officer Total employee count
4. Steps for Assigning MDO Role
1. Identify Place of Postings
Ensure postings are under the administrative control of the MDO.
Multiple MDO roles may be created based on different postings.
2. Nomination of Officer
Submit authorization/nomination letter approved by the Competent Authority.
Officer should preferably not be below the rank of Deputy Secretary/Director.
3. Indicate Place of Postings
Clearly specify postings covered under the MDO role in the nomination letter.
4. ransfer of MDO Role
In case of transfer/reshuffling, the authorized officer must inform DoP&T
immediately.
Access to the MDO role will be stopped without delay.
5. Steps for Assigning CCA Role
1. Nomination of Officers (Write Rights)
Competent Authority sends a letter to DoP&T.
Eligible officers: Under Secretary or above (Level-11 or higher).
2. Nomination of Officers (Read Rights)
Details of officers for read-only rights included in the same letter.
Eligible officers: Section Officer or above (Level-8 or higher).
3. Transfer of CCA Role
Transfer/reshuffling order suffices; no separate DoP&T approval required.
4. Service Mapping
 
Clearly name the service against which the role is to be assigned.
If a new service is to be created, a letter must be sent for service creation.
6. Steps for Assigning AVD Admin Role
1. Nomination by Competent Authority
Submit a formal letter nominating the officer for the AVD Admin role and service
against which this role is assigned.
2. Role Assignment
Once approved by the DoPT tech team will assign the AVD Admin role upon
receipt of nomination.
Officer will be responsible for the updation of vigilance/disciplinary status in e-
HRMS 2.0.
3. Transfer of Role
In case of transfer/reshuffling, the concerned MDO must notify DoP&T
immediately for role deactivation and reassignment.
7. Training & Support
Demo and training sessions are being conducted to support Ministries in onboarding
and deployment of e-HRMS 2.0.
Participation details will be shared separately.
8. Compliance & Timelines
MDOs are requested to complete the process at the earliest.
Ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with prescribed formats for smooth
onboarding.
9. Nominations to be Shared on following ids
 
1. support.ehrms-dopt@gov.in
2. ehrms-dopt@gov.in
3. cto-karmayogi@gov.in
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) – Onboarding & Nominations under e-
HRMS 2.0
1. What is e-HRMS 2.0?
e-HRMS 2.0 is an end-to-end online Human Resource Management System
launched by the Government of India to provide services such as leave,
reimbursement, training, and other HR modules for government employees.
2. What information must Ministries/Departments/Organisations (MDOs) provide
for onboarding?
MDOs must share:
Number of Current Places of Postings Along with Nodal Officers Nominations
In-position Strength
3. Who can be appointed as a Nodal Officer?
The officer should belong to Administration/Establishment and be closely
monitoring Service Books.
Appointment must be endorsed by the Competent Authority through a
supporting letter.
Details required: Name, Designation, Date of Birth, Father’s Name, Official
Email ID (gov.in/nic.in), Mobile Number, MDO Name, Place of Posting, and
Number of Employees under the officer.
4. How should employee details be submitted?
Use the prescribed Excel template “Template – Onboarding Employees.”
Mandatory fields: Employee Name (without salutation), Father’s Name, Date of
Birth (dd-mm-yyyy), Designation, Email ID, Mobile Number.
Populate details for all employees under the Department/Ministry.
5. What is the onboarding process for employees?
1. Fill mandatory fields in the template.
2. Populate details for all employees.
3. Technical team will onboard employees and confirm to the Department.
4. Employees must complete their profiles on the e-HRMS 2.0 Portal.
5. Employees can then access services such as Leave, Reimbursement, Training,
etc.
6. How is the MDO role assigned?
 
Identify the Place of Postings under the administrative control of the MDO.
Submit an authorization/nomination letter approved by the Competent Authority.
Officer should preferably not be below the rank of Deputy Secretary/Director.
Clearly specify postings covered under the MDO role.
In case of transfer/reshuffling, the authorized officer must inform DoP&T
immediately for role deactivation.
7. How is the CCA role assigned?
Write Rights: Competent Authority sends a letter to DoP&T nominating officers
of Under Secretary or above (Level-11 or higher).
Read Rights: Same letter may include officers of Section Officer or above
(Level-8 or higher).
Transfer: Transfer/reshuffling order suffices; no separate DoP&T approval
required.
Service Mapping: Clearly name the service against which the role is to be
assigned. If a new service is required, a letter must be sent for service creation.
8. How is the AVD Admin role assigned?
Competent Authority submits a formal nomination letter.
Once approved, the DoP&T technical team assigns the role.
Officer will be responsible for updating vigilance/disciplinary status in e-HRMS
2.0.
In case of transfer/reshuffling, MDO must notify DoP&T immediately for role
deactivation and reassignment.
9. Is training provided for e-HRMS 2.0?
Yes. Demo and training sessions are being conducted to support Ministries in
onboarding and deployment. Participation details will be shared separately. Training
requests to be shared on the following emails;
1. cto-karmayogi@gov.in
2. ehrms-dopt@gov.in
3. sheetal.saini@karmayogi.in
4. taranpal.singh@karmayogi.in
5. aquib.khan@karmayogi.in
6. tyagi.priyanka@karmayogi.in
10. Where should nominations and details be sent?
All nominations and required details must be shared at the following email IDs:
1. support.ehrms-dopt@gov.in
2. ehrms-dopt@gov.in
3. cto-karmayogi@gov.in

"Thank you to the DoPT eHRMS team for taking out time to train us on the application in very detailed manner

"Serving as MDO-Admin (eHRMS) at ICAR over the past three years has been a highly rewarding journey. With
continuous support from DoPT, Karmayogi Bharat, and the eHRMS team, ICAR successfully strengthened eHRMS

eSAMARTH with eHRMS, enabling seamless management of employee financial records. These initiatives

stakeholders who contributed to this successful transformation."

“I am an e-HRMS user, and I feel that e-HRMS 2.0 has made leave management simpler, faster, and more
transparent. The deemed approval feature is especially beneficial, as leave requests no longer remain pending for
an indefinite period, and employees receive timely decisions without the need for repeated follow-ups. It enhances
accountability, minimizes administrative delays, and gives employees greater confidence in the leave approval
process.”
Pranay Ranjan, ASO
“The e-HRMS 2.0 mobile app has made routine HR services more convenient and accessible. I can access
important information and complete basic HR-related tasks on the go, without having to depend on a desktop or
office system. This helps save time, reduces the need for repeated follow-ups, and makes everyday HR services
simpler and easier to access.
The continued initiative towards making HR services more accessible through digital and mobile platforms is much
appreciated. I hope the e-HRMS 2.0 mobile app will continue to evolve with further enhancements and the
introduction of more useful and employee-centric features in the future.”
Department of Commerce

In fact CGHS caters to the healthcare needs of eligible beneficiaries covering all four pillars of democratic set up in India namely Legislature, Judiciary, Executive and Press. Presently approximately 42 lakh beneficiaries are covered by CGHS in 80 cities all over India and the endeavour is to include more cities to improve the accessibility of the services. Vision To be the first choice in providing quality healthcare services and ensuring holistic well being across clients' entire life span. Mission Preventive, promotive and curative health and wellness services that are responsive, accountable and cost effective, providing financial risk protection and ensuring healthy lives. 2. On the Personal Device Config screen, following options are present :: 
 
All the below parameters combine to create the Geo Policy for the Organisation and 
related Personal Device 
Nodal Officer to Ensure that Update button is clicked so that latest policy is available 
 
 
 
 
The Parameters are described :: 
 
a. GeoFence Enforce 
i. Value Yes : It restricts all the employees within the organisation 
to mark attendance within the Geo fenced periphery 
 Nodal to set the permitted Distance within which employee would be 
allowed to mark attendance. 
 
ii. Value No : Allows all the employees within the organisation to 
mark attendance from any location. 
 
 
b. Distance ( In Meter ) : 
This option would be activated only when the Nodal has selected 
GeoFence Enforce as Yes. 
 

 
3 | A E B A S 
***** This application  and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
 
 
 
i. Nodal to set the permitted Distance within which employee 
would be allowed to mark attendance. 
ii. The value should be greater than 0 
 
 
c. Only Self Attendance 
i. Value Yes : Restrict the Personal Device to be used by an 
individual Employee and associated attendance ID ONLY. 
 
ii. Value No : Allow the Personal Device of an employee to be 
used by other employees of the Organisation. 
 
 
d. Entry point change by Employee 
i. Value Yes : Allows employee to change the Entry point if 
available. 
ii. Value No : Restricts the employee marking attendance for a 
particular entry point only. 
 
 
e. Attendance allowed from other locations 
This facility is synonym for Roaming Facility for a set of employees 
 
i. Value Yes : The Nodal officer would allow a set of employees to 
mark attendance on Roaming. 
In order to use this option, Nodal officer to create a Roaming 
List for the same 
( May refer Annexure : A ) 
 
ii. Value No : The Nodal Officer does not allow any one to mark 
attendance in Roaming Option

***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
 ATTENDANCE MARKING THROUGH FACE RECOGNITION on :: 
PERSONAL MOBILE 
 
AEBAS team has created software for FACE based Aadhaar authentication with 
UIDAI RD for attendance marking through Face Recognition. For face 
authentication, picture from the repository of CIDR of UIDAI would be used. In this 
process face biometric would be used in place of Fingerprint/Iris of the individual.  
 
The application would work in the similar fashion as earlier with the only difference 
that individual’s face would be used.  
Earlier the attendance marking was facilitated through Biometric i.e. Fingerprint or 
Iris.  
Keeping in mind the current situation where the world is in the middle of a 
pandemic, the attendance marking has now been initiated through Face.  
 
The process for attendance marking would remain the same, where in the user 
would input his/her attendance ID and would be prompted to show the face.  
On successful attendance marking, the display would show attendance opening 
and/or attendance closing for that particular employee  
 
The application is available for Android devices only (minimum requirement stated 
in the document).  
Installation process for the same is explained below  
If your attendance marking ID is 6- digit / 8-digit refer Annexure – A  
 
In case of any query please contact: 1800 111 555 or raise ticket at 
https://servicedesk.nic.in/ 
 
General Attendance Marking Guidelines:  
1. The individual marking attendance should ensure that there is Good Light on the 
face.  
2. User should follow all the instructions shown on the RD screen.  
3. There should not be any multiple objects/persons in the background.  
 
 
Minimum Device Specification:  
Android version above 9, RAM 4+GB, Camera 5 MP and above. 
ioS software version 14 and above 
  
 
 
2 | A E B A S  
***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
Installation application initial steps: 
 
1. Download and Install the Aadhaar Face RD APP from the Google Play 
Store/AppStore. 
 
 
 
2. Download and Install the AadhaarBAS App from the Google Play 
Store/AppStore. 
 
 
 
 May please refer Annexure -A for further action

Employee Login:

 You may check it in employee login in the attendance portal 
 If office location incorrect, may please update the office location 
 
** Ensure that latest versions of AadhaarFaceRD and AadhaarBAS App are 
installed/used for usage of APP.

***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME

Android 
 
1. Open the FACE BAS APP

2. Select the Domain in which attendance is required to be marked (i.e. Delhi 
Central; attendance.gov.in /Central; central.attendance.gov.in/ 
States/Schemes) 
 
 
  

 
 
5 | A E B A S  
***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
3. Enter the attendance ID, in which the employee is registered (i.e. if Delhi 
Central 6 digit attendanceID ; or Central/State, etc.; central.attendance.gov.in, 
8 digit attendanceID) and click on Submit 
 
 
 
 
 
  

 
 
6 | A E B A S  
***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
4. Choose the Entry point from where the employee will mark attendance. 
 
          
 
 
  

 
 
7 | A E B A S  
***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
 
To know your Geo Lat Long use the may please download the app present in 
your Employee Login: 
 https://attendance.gov.in/update/employee/entryPoint 
Visit Organization URL. 
 
************ 
In case, if latitude - longitude not configured with your entry point. Share 
your Attendance_ID, Employee Name, OfficeLocation, GPS Lat-Long, Entry 
Point (Contact the Org Nodal Officer) 
 
Ensure the “Scan Biometric” is clicked and authentication is completed. 
 
 
 
  

 
 
8 | A E B A S  
***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
 
5.  Attendance Marking screen will be prompted.  
Ensure that the checkbox is clicked. 
 
                     
  
111222

***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
 
6. User will show the face and attendance will be marked 
 
      
 
7. The attendance is successfully marked and the Attendance In/out would be 
recorded

***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
8. Geo- Fencing Policy Update :: 
 
Click on the 3 dots, on the extreme right panel to check for the geo fencing policy 
update 
 
 
 
May click on “Update Geofencing Policy”, if update is available, the policy will be 
updated

***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME

Click on the 3 dots, on the extreme right panel to check for the Change of Device 
Location

Choose the Device Location from the list specified 
          
 
Save the location , the status will be updated on the user screen: 
10. Notifications 
Click on the 3 dots, on the extreme right panel to check for the Notifications 
Settings 
 
 

 
 
13 | A E B A S  
***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME 
 
This feature would allow the user to set the notification for Attendance Marking 
time in the morning and evening. 
By using this feature, the user can set the time for which the notification is desired. 
 
9-+ 
 
All the options chosen should be saved for successful notification on the user device. 
  
A. User to choose if the notification is required  
B. User to select the days for which the 
notification is required.  
C. User to mention the start time and end time 
for morning notification and evening 
notification 
Based on this the notification would be sent to 
the user 
D. User to mention the office WiFi IPs, if the 
attendance is to be marked within the office 
network. 
 
 
14 | A E B A S  
***** This application and RD are only for Internal Use. DO NOT SHARE THE SAME

All the Attendance marked on the personal device only would be shown with the

In this case the attendance would be recorded as Roaming and same would be 
displayed in the Nodal Login. 
 
13. Re-Register Device  
If the Employee has been transferred from Central to the State, the employee can 
now re-register the device with the attendance ID and mark attendance post 
successful registration of the device.

No. 22003/208/CPGRAMS/2025-I4C
Government of India
Ministry of Home Affairs
Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)

5" floor, NDCC-II Building

Jai ages Road, New Delhi

Dated:,4& January, 2026
PUBLIC NOTICE

Subject: Information regarding implementation of Grievance Redressal
Mechanism under CPGRAMS.

The Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) is an
online platform available to citizens 24x7 to lodge grievances to public authorities on
any subject related to service delivery. It aims to promote a responsive, transparent, and
accountable administration.

2s The I4C under the Ministry of Home Affairs, functions as a research and
coordination body dedicated to strengthening the national framework for combating
cybercrime. The I4C is committed to the effective redressal of public grievances in letter
and spirit. Experience has shown that when an applicant approaches the correct Public
Authority, it significantly expedites the resolution process. Therefore, it is essential to
apprise citizens about the operational ambit of I4C concerning the redressal of
grievances.

3. Following issues are worth mentioning in this context:

i. ‘Police’ and 'Public Order' are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule
of the Constitution of India and States/UTs are primarily responsible for
prevention, detection, and investigation of all crimes including cybercrime
through their Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAS).

ii. I4C is not an investigative agency. The complaints received on National

Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP) are investigated by the Law

 
iii.

Vi.

Enforcement Agencies (LEA) of State/UT concerned and not by I4C as it
does not possess the powers of investigation under the Bhartiya Nagarik
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS). Accordingly, the custodian of information
available on NCRP or other portals like Sahyog, Samanvaya etc. are Law
Enforcement Agencies of States/UTs I4C manages only the technical
infrastructure related to NCRP. The status of investigation is also updated
on NCRP by LEAs of States/UTs from time to time. All complainants can
see the status of their complaint by visiting NCRP.

The lien marking/freezing of bank account is not done by I4C, MHA. The
decision to lien mark/freeze a bank account is either taken by the
Investigating Officer of LEA concerned under the provision of BNS/BNSS
on the basis of investigation and evidences or by the bank officials under
various regulations of RBI.

Likewise, the blocking of mobile numbers and devices is also done by
LEAs of  States/UTs under the appropriate provisions of
Telecommunications Act, 2023 and rules made there under along with
BNS/BNSS and not by I4C.

Accordingly, all grievances relating to State Governments, Union Territory
Administrations, and the Government of NCT of Delhi are to be redressed
by the respective State/UT Government through their Law Enforcement
Agencies (LEA).

As I4C functions as a national-level coordination centre, grievances
received on CPGRAMS that pertain to specific incidents of cybercrime or
local law enforcement matters are forwarded/transferred to the concerned

State/UT nodal authorities for appropriate action.

4. In view of the above cited facts, the general public is hereby informed:

i;

To file grievance applications with appropriate public authorities of
States/UTs in case they desire information regarding investigations
undertaken or portal-specific operational data (National Cybercrime

Reporting Portal data).

 
a

iii.

a)

b)

०)

qd)

e)

Citizens may track the status of their grievances using the unique
registration ID provided at the time of lodging the complaint on

https://pgportal.gov.in/Status.

Exclusions from CPGRAMS: As per DARPG comprehensive guidelines
dated 23.08.2024 available on https://pgportal.gov.in under ‘What’s New’,

the following categories of grievances are not permissible for redressal
under this platform:

Sub-judice Matters: Any case currently under consideration by a court of
law or matters concerning judgments already delivered by a court.
Personal Disputes: Issues involving personal or family feuds and private
disputes.

RTI Matters: Queries or complaints relating to the Right to Information
Act (which should be handled via the dedicated RTI portal).

National Security: Matters impacting the territorial integrity of the country
or friendly relations with foreign nations.

Service Matters: As mentioned in the DoPT’s O.M. No. 03/08/20I3-
Estt(A-III) dated 3.8.205, the grievances regarding service matters shall

not be submitted on this platform.

This notice is issued to facilitate the effective implementation of the grievance

redressal mechanism and to ensure that citizens' concerns reach the rightful redressal

office for prompt resolution.

The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) has observed a rise in 
financial frauds perpetrated through  malicious Android application s masquerading as  
pornography apps, circulated through Facebook and Instagram ads operating under the names 
"Night Play", "Reloop", "Kyss", “Vimo”, “Rivo”, “Nexo”, “Vixa” and other similar variants.  
These applications are primarily distributed through advertisements on Facebook and 
Instagram, which redirect to websites serving pornographic content, where the user is prompted 
to download the  APK. After installation, the app  requests permissions that allow it to  install 
additional applications and by abusing accessibility permission, take control of the users’ device, 
which may result in financial fraud . Some apps also install a VPN, which may be used to route 
internet traffic pertaining to  malicious/criminal activity.  The app may prevent users from 
uninstalling it through the device settings.  
 
  
                                                                          
ADVISORY     
TAU/ADV/018 | Dated 26th August 2026 
Malicious Side Loaded Pornographic Android Apps leading to Unauthorized 
Financial Transactions 
Modus operandi of fraud through malicious sideloaded pornographic Android apps 
National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU)    
Indian
 Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), MHA 

 
MODUS OPERANDI 
1. Distribution: The malicious application is distributed through pornographic content 
related advertisements or links majorly on Facebook and Instagram. These ads redirect 
to phishing websites.  
2. Redirection: Ads redirect to phishing websites serving pornographic content. Domains of 
the website majorly belong to “.live”. Users are persuaded to download and install the APK 
from sources outside the Google Play Store.  
3. App Update: A secondary package gets downloaded and installed on the pretext of an 
app update, based on permissions abused by the first, initial app.     
4. Abuse of Accessibility Permission for d evice takeover: After installation, the 
application asks users to grant Accessibility and other sensitive permissions. Once 
enabled, the malware gains control of the device and continues to run in the background.  
5. VPN Installation: Some apps may also install a VPN on the device, thereby routing all 
internet traffic through attacker-controlled servers. This compromises user's transmitted 
data, which may subsequently be exploited for malicious or criminal activities. 
6. Unauthorized Transactions: Since the malware has the ability to take over the  
compromised device, installing such appsmay lead to fianancial fraud.  
 
PRECAUTIONS AND SAFETY RECOMMENDATIONS 
 Install applications only from Google Play Store or other trusted app stores. 
 Do not download APK files from advertisements, websites or suspicious links. 
 Do not enable/grant Accessibility permission for unknown applications. 
 Review installed applications and remove any application you do not recognize. 
 Keep Google Play Protect enabled and keep your Android device updated. 
 Check your bank account and UPI transactions regularly. 
STEPS TO UNINSTALL 
METHOD 1: SAFE MODE REBOOT 
Step 1: Start Your Phone in Safe Mode : Press and hold the Power butto n. Press and hold 
Power Off until the Safe Mode option appears. Click OK or Restart in Safe Mode. Wait for the 
phone to restart. "Safe Mode" will appear at the bottom of the screen. 
Step 2: Uninstall the App: Open Settings. Go to Apps. Select the suspicious application. Tap 
Uninstall. Remove any other unknown or related applications. 
Step 3: Restart Normally: Restart the phone. The device will exit Safe Mode automatically. 
 
National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU)    
Indian
 Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), MHA 
 
ANOTHER METHOD  
Step 1: Restore the Default Home Screen (If required): Open Settings. Go to Apps → Default 
Apps → Home App.  Select your phone's original launcher (System Launcher, One UI Home, 
Pixel Launcher, etc.). 
Step 2: Disable Accessibility Access : Open Settings. Tap Accessibility. Open Installed 
Services or Downloaded Apps. Select the suspicious application. Turn Accessibility Off. 
Step 3: Remove Administrator Access: Open Settings. Go to Security or Security & Privacy. 
Open Device Admin Apps or Device Administrators.  If the suspicious app is enabled, select it.  
Tap Deactivate or Turn Off. 
 
Verify the Device : Open Settings > Apps. Confirm that the suspicious application has been 
removed. If the app cannot be removed or returns after restarting, back up your important data 
and perform a Factory Reset. 
 
Report any fraudulent applications or any scam incident immediately on 1930 or

भारत 2026 के स्वागत और 20df सदी की दूसरी तिमाही में कदम Nad हुए
विकस्नमित भारत बनने की अपनी यात्रा के सबसे महत्वपूर्ण ck में प्रवेश कर रहा है।
राष्ट्रीय पुनरूत्थान की इस यात्रा की राह में समुद्रों का महत्व लगातार बढ़ रहा है जो
कि समुद्री क्षेत्रों की सुरक्षा, संरक्षा और स्थिरता का आघार है। भारत की समुद्री शक्ति
के WR साधन और प्रत्यक्ष प्रमाण के रूप में भारतीय नौसेना हमारे देश के सुरक्षित
समुद्री भविष्य का अग्रणी गारंटर है।

बीते वर्ष में, जब, जहां, जैसी जरूरत हुई, अपनी ब्यूटी करने में हमने अतिस्रक्रिय
तत्परता तथा Actes कार्यवाही का प्रदर्शन किया है ।मिशन पर तैनात हमारी यूनिटों ने
अपने क्षेत्र में तथा उससे बाहर भी बदलते परिदृश्य में पेशेवर कुशलता और गर्व के साथ
ate सुरक्षा साझेदार एवं फर्स्ट रेस्पोंडः के रूप में हमारा मान-सम्मान बढ़ाया है। साथ
ही बेहतर सक्षमता के समावेश एवं स्वदेशी प्रौद्योगिकियों के विकास से हमारी ऑपेशनल
तत्परता को मजबूती मिली है और हमारी युद्धक se को बल मिला है।

आगे बढ़ते हुए ' लक्ष्य पर आयुध '(ऑर्डनेन्स ऑन टार्गेट) की सटीक डिलीवरी सुनिश्चित
करके, ऑपरेशन संबंधी तत्परता लाकर और सभी क्षेत्रों में संयोजन और एकीकरण बढ़ाकर
हमें अपनी युद्धक दक्षता और बेहतर करनी है। निरंतर सुधार करने वाले एक संगठन
के रूप में विकसित होते रहने के अपने संकल्प पर हमें अडिग रहना है और अपनी
संगठनात्मक संस्कृति के एक अटल पक्ष के तौर पर संरक्षा और सुरक्षा के उच्चतम मानक
बनाए रखना है। प्रशिक्षण, नेतृत्व क्षमता और पेशेवर उत्कृष्टता के लिए प्रतिबद्ध रहकर हमें
समुद्र में और जमीन पर अपने कार्यकलाप ड्यूटी, सम्मान और साहस के बुनियादी मूल्यों
की राह पर जारी रखने हैं।

में टीम नेवी के प्रत्येक वर्दीधारी एवं सिविलियन सदस्य से राष्ट्र और नौसेना की

बरकरार रखें जो हमारे समुद्री हितों को कभी भी, कहीं भी, कैसे भी सुरक्षित रुवने के
लिए सदेव तैयार है।

मुझे पूरा विश्वास है कि आने वाले वर्ष में भी हमारे सामूहिक प्रयासों से राष्ट्र एवं भारतीय

MESSAGE FROM THE CHIEF OF THE NAVAL STAFF

As we welcome 2026 and usher in the second quarter of the
Twenty-First Century, India is entering one of the most defining
periods in its journey to become Viksit Bharat. This voyage of
national resurgence is increasingly shaped by the seas and, is
founded ona safe, secure and stable maritime domain. The Indian
Navy, as the prime instrument and principal manifestation of
India’s maritime power, remains the foremost guarantor of our
nation’s seaborne future.

In the year gone by, we have demonstrated proactive
readiness and purposeful action, meeting our mandate
whenever and wherever required. Our mission deployed units
have responded to emerging scenarios with professionalism
and pride, reinforcing our stature as a Preferred Security Partner
and First Responder in the region and beyond. At the same time,
the induction of cutting-edge capabilities and advancement of
indigenous technologies have strengthened our operational
readiness and sustained our combat edge.

As we propel ahead, we must continue to sharpen our
warfighting proficiency by ensuring accurate delivery of
‘Ordnance on Target’, embracing operational agility, and
deepening jointness and integration across all domains.
We remain steadfast in our resolve to evolve as a Learning
Organisation, and uphold the highest standards of Safety and
Security as an enduring facet of our organisational culture.
Through commitment to training, leadership and professional
excellence, our conduct, at sea and ashore, must continue to
exemplify the core values of Duty, Honour, Courage.

I call upon every member of Team Navy - both uniformed
and civilian, to rededicate themselves in service of the Navy and
the Nation. Let us continue to nurture a Combat Ready, Credible,
Cohesive and Future Ready Indian Navy, that is prepared to
safeguard our national maritime interests - Anytime, Anywhere,
Anyhow.

I am confident that with our collective efforts, the year
ahead would see India and the Indian Navy achieve greater
success. I wish the entire Team Navy good health, happiness
and prosperity in 2026.

Jai Hind! Sam No Varunah!

pe See
(Dinesh K Tripathi)

Candidates working in Government / Semi Government / Public Undertakings / Autonomous bodies should

Only screened in applicants will be called for Level - written test. Only shortlisted candidates as explained

Candidates are required to have a valid Email ID and Mobile Number & convey the same in the application. It
should be kept active during the currency of this recruitment. IMSc will send intimation / call letters for written
examination only through the registered email ID.

Any subsequent amendments / modifications etc. on this matter will be notified only in IMSc website under the
page “Recruitment of Upper Division Clerk” under Other Positions under Opportunities page which may
be referred to by the candidates regularly.

At the time of written examination, candidates must bring a printout of the call letter sent to them through email
printed properly with header.

Before applying for the post, candidates should ensure that they fulfill all the eligibility norms. Candidates
should have the requisite Educational & other Qualifications from recognised University / Institute as on the
date of submission of the application.

Mere fulfillment of requirements as laid down in the Advertisement does not entitle a candidate to be called for
written examination. Incomplete applications shall be summarily rejected.

OBC Certificate should be issued by the Specified Authority in the prescribed format and the Caste /
Community should have been included in the Central lists of OBC in relation to the concerned state. For
claiming the benefit of reservation the OBC candidates are required to submit a latest Caste Certificate (Non-
creamy layer) covering the financial year of the advertisement in the proforma prescribed by Govenment of
India and upload along with their online application. The Certificate submitted for claiming reservation under
OBC category should have a mention that the candidate does not belong to the persons / sections (Creamy

 
layer) as mentioned in Col. (3) of Schedule to the Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India
OM NO. 36022/22/93-Estt.(SCT) dated 8.9.93 and OM No. 36033/I/203-Estt.(Res.) dated 3.9.207. The
candidates belonging to OBC category but falling in creamy layer are not entitled to OBC reservation benefits.

2. The prescribed qualification are minimum and mere possession of the same does not entitle candidates to be
called for Level - 4 written test. The decision of the Director of this Institute in all matters will be final and
binding on the candidates and no enquiry or correspondence will be entertained in this matter.

3. The selected candidates will be governed by new re-structured defined contribution Pension Scheme (National
Pension Scheme), which has come into force w.e.f. ..2004 vide Ministry of Finance Notification No. 5/7/2003-
ECB&PR dated 22.2.2003 and the provisions made there under by contributing monthly an amount of 0% of
pay and Dearness allowances and 4% contribution from Government.

4. Probation : The persons selected will be appointed on probation as per rules.

5. IMSc reserves the right to accept or reject any application at any stage of the Recruitment process, if the
candidate is found ineligible for the post. The decision of Director, IMSc shall be final in deciding the eligibility
of the candidate. The mere fact that a call letter has been issued to the candidate and allowed to appear in
written examination will not imply that his / her candidature has been finally cleared or that entries made by the
candidate in his / her application have been accepted as true and correct.

I6. Director, IMSc reserves the right to cancel the whole process of recruitment without assigning any reasons.

7. Evaluation of answer papers of Level - test will be completed and results will be published on the IMSc
website. Therefore, the candidates need not wait for the declaration of the result at test venue and they are
advised to keep checking the IMSc web-site.

8. Decision of the Director, IMSc will be final in all respects.

9. The validity of operation of wait list, if drawn, will be one year from the date of preparation of the Select Panel.
The wait listed candidate will be offered the post only in case of non joining of selected candidate / resignation
of selected candidate after joining the post within one year from the date of drawal of the wait list.

20. Record of the non selected candidates shall not be preserved beyond 6 months from the date of formation of
select list.

1. Introduction 
1.1. Aims and Objective 
1.1.1. The Vision of the scheme is “to transform India’s Sports Landscape”. 
1.1.2. Khelo India Scheme (2026- 27 to 2030- 31) focuses on achieving Nation’s 
Excellence on the Global Stage by enhancing infrastructure, talent identification 
& development, and international competitiveness. It aims to strengthen India’s 
sports ecosystem through world- class infrastructure, structured competitions, 
nationwide training facilities, scientific talent identification, coaching 
excellence, competitive pathways, fitness promotion, and measures across 
initiatives to create a robust, inclusive and globally competitive sports culture 
that positions India as a leading force in the international sporting arena.  
1.1.3. Aligned with Khelo Bharat Niti- 2025 and National Education Policy (NEP) 
2020, the scheme integrat es sports with education to nurture holistic 
development and life skills in students, youths, promoting both academic and 
athletic excellence. Leveraging technology and data -driven governance, the 
scheme positions sports as a catalyst for national pride, soc ial integration, and 
economic growth. 
1.1.4. The Khelo India Scheme aims to operationalise the components of the scheme 
with convergent use of various schemes of the M inistry, other Ministries or 
Departments of the Government of India, States/UTs, institutions, MPLADS, 
MLALADS, CSR initiatives, public or private entities, PPP models, and 
corporate sponsorships. The  Scheme envisages innovation at the local level 
keeping in view the broad national perspective of making sporting a mass 
movement and promoting excellence in sports.  Such support shall be clearly 
disclosed, approvals to be taken where required, and used to supplement Scheme 
assistance without duplication of funding for the same activity or expenditure. 
 
1.2. Scheme Components 
1.2.1. The Khelo India Scheme shall comprise the following nine components: 
a. Sports Infrastructure for Medal Strategy 
b. Strengthening Strategic Sports Assets 
 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 6 
 
c. State Action Plan for Sports Infrastructure Development 
d. Sports Competitions & Leagues 
e. Talent Identification and Development 
f. Coach & Support Staff Development 
g. Khelo India Training Facilities 
h. Fit India Movement 
i. Sports Technology 
1.2.2. All 9 components of Khelo India Scheme (2026-27 to 2030- 31) will be 
implemented through Sports Authority of India /any other body/organisation 
designated by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. 
 
1.3. Priority Disciplines 
1.3.1. As part of the Scheme, all the major sports disciplines under Olympic s/Asian 
Games/Other Major international competitions shall be considered for broad -
basing of talent. However, the following 18 Sports disciplines shall be 
considered as Priority Sports: 
a. Aquatics 
b. Archery 
c. Athletics 
d. Badminton 
e. Boxing 
f. Canoeing 
g. Cycling 
h. Gymnastics 
i. Hockey 
j. Judo 
k. Rowing 
l. Shooting 
m. Squash 
n. Table Tennis 
o. Taekwondo 
p. Tennis

q. Weightlifting 
r. Wrestling 
 
1.4. Approval Mechanism 
1.4.1. All the proposals will be appraised by Project Appraisal Committee (PAC) from 
administrative, financial and utility angles along with the past performance. The 
recommendations of the PAC will be placed before the Departmental Project 
Approval Committee (DPAC) chaired by the Secretary, Department of Sports, 
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS), Government of India, for the 
final decision. 
  
 

 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 9 
 
2. Sports Infrastructure for Medal Strategy 
2.1. Introduction 
2.1.1. The Component of Sports Infrastructure for Medal Strategy under Khelo India 
Scheme aims at providing support for creating and upgrading WUDLQLQJဩFHQWULF 
sports infrastructure required for augmenting the medal prospects in sports 
disciplines which are part of Olympics/Asian Games/ O ther Major international 
competitions.   
 
2.2. Proposals 
2.2.1. The component will support brownfield and greenfield projects, including fields 
of play, hostels, strength and conditioning facilities, sports science centres, allied 
support infrastructure, and repair and maintenance of underutilized assets, with 
dedicated operations and maintenance funding as required , equipment etc . 
Preference would be given to brownfield projects. 
2.2.2. Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) / Sports Authority of India (SAI) 
will conduct gap analysis along with relevant stakeholders including  National 
Sports Federation (NSF) and identify facilities/regions  where sports specific 
infrastructure needs to be upgraded/created. 
2.2.3. Projects will be selected and prioritised through stakeholder consultation, field 
studies and gap analysis to address infrastructure gaps and talent potential, linking 
facilities with competitive pathways to support athletes from grassroots to elite 
levels. 
2.2.4. Suitable entities (central/state government/other institutions) shall be identified to 
receive assistance for the creation and upgradation of sports infrastructure under 
this component. The identified entities shall be encouraged to submit proposals as 
per the notified norms and criteria. 
 
2.3. Receipt of Proposals 
2.3.1. The proposals shall be obtained in the form of a Project Report (PR) from suitable 
entities which shall include (but not limited to) the following details: 
a. Application in the format prescribed by MYAS. 
 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 10 
 
b. Estimates of cost – All costs must be as per the latest Delhi Schedule of 
Rates/Central Public Works Department (CPWD) rates updated with the Cost 
Indices of the particular State/UT.  
c. Confirmation that the land on which the proposed project is to be executed is 
free from all encumbrances. Clear documentation establishing 
ownership/lease to be enclosed along with the proposal. 
d. A comprehensive utilisation  and O&M roadmap covering institutional 
arrangements, coaches/trainers and support staff, annual training and 
competition calendar, athlete intake and usage, equipment procurement and 
upkeep, boarding and lodging, eligible -user access, and measures for 
sustained year-round use shall be submitted by the grantee in alignment with 
Scheme objectives.  Suitable plans may be explored by a pplicants for 
inclusion of revenue mobilization framework to offset recurring O&M costs 
and reduce net fiscal burden. 
2.3.2. All the infrastructure created /upgraded shall incorporate the following 
mechanisms: 
a. Follow the harmonized guidelines of accessible sports complex and 
residential facilities for para -athletes conceptualized as per applicable 
guidelines issued from time to time. 
b. Optimum utilisation of resources  including measures  such as  usage of 
renewable energy, rainwater harvesting,  LED lights, enhancing water use 
efficiency, consideration of the overall carbon footprint across the lifecycle 
of the facility etc., as feasible.  
c. Good practices such as usage of local building materials, recycling of 
Construction & Demolition waste etc. is encouraged as far as possible. 
2.3.3. The infrastructure created/upgraded shall be disaster resilient as per National 
Building Construction Standards 2026 Code (designated as SP 7:2026) and IS 
code 1893:2025 and/or their latest revision as applicable. It shall be mandatory to 
adhere to the Environmental Guidelines and/or their latest revision as applicable 
in the concerned State/UT. 
2.3.4. Sports infrastructure created /upgraded under the Scheme shall be utilised in 
accordance with the MoU between MYAS and the grantee, ensuring alignment 
 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 11 
 
with the component’s objectives. The facility shall be used judiciously ensuring 
optimal utilisation.  
2.3.5. All sports infrastructure projects funded under this Scheme should mandatorily 
include “Khelo India” in the displayed signage and other relevant branding 
guidelines issued by the Ministry from time to time. 
2.3.6. The suitable entities shall forward their proposals, along with additional relevant 
documents in a physical/hard copy to MYAS. On activation of the Khel Setu, all 
new proposals shall be submitted digitally.  
 
2.4. Appraisal and Approval 
2.4.1. All proposals shall undergo a structured appraisal process to ensure technical  
soundness, fiscal prudence, and alignment with scheme objectives. 
2.4.2. Preliminary Scrutiny: MYAS shall examine completeness of documentation, 
eligibility of the implementing agency and conformity with infrastructure 
classification norms. 
2.4.3. Only such proposals, which are complete in all respects and technically feasible, 
will be considered for sanction. Suitable feasibility report based on necessity will 
be obtained. 
2.4.4. Technical and Financial Appraisal: Technical appraisal shall assess compliance of 
the Field of Play with approved standards and norms, appropriateness of ancillary 
facilities, and feasibility of implementation timelines. Financial appraisal shall 
assess cost reasonableness, proportionality of components, funding commitments, 
and sustainability of operations and maintenance arrangements. 
2.4.5. Appraisal by Project Appraisal Committee (PAC): Proposals found suitable shall 
be placed before the Project Appraisal Committee (PAC), which shall examine the 
proposal in totality and record its recommendations. The PAC may recommend 
approval, approval with modifications, or rejection.  
2.4.6. Departmental Project Approval Committee (DPAC): Recommendations of the 
PAC shall be placed before the Departmental Project Approval  Committee 
(DPAC) headed by the Secretary (Sports) for approval. DPAC may consider 
technical, financial, utilisation and strategic aspects before according approval.

DPAC may periodically review the utilisation and performance of the facilities 
sanctioned.  
2.4.7. The detailed approval and monitoring mechanism shall be as per Chapter 12 of 
the Operation Guidelines of the scheme. 
2.4.8. Administrative and Financial Sanction: Upon approval by DPAC, a formal 
administrative approval shall be issued in alignment with the provisions of the MoU.  
2.4.9. Wherever feasible convergence or co -funding be undertaken with other schemes 
of the Ministry, other Ministries or Departments of the Government of India, 
States/UTs, institutions, MPLADS, MLALADS, CSR initiatives, public or private 
entities, PPP models, and corporate sponsorships. Such support shall be clearly 
disclosed, approvals to be taken where required, and used to supplement Scheme 
assistance without duplication of funding for the same activity or expenditure.

5. Sports Competitions and Leagues 
5.1. Introduction 
5.1.1. Sports Competitions and leagues will support talent identification, athlete 
monitoring, performance benchmarking, and progression to national and 
international excellence. The initiative will also strengthen officiating, technical 
expertise, Games management, and institutional coordination while expanding 
participation across all States and UTs, with special emphasis on increasing 
participation and performance opportunities for women, para -athletes, and 
athletes from tribal, remote border, North-Eastern regions, and others. 
5.1.2. Sports that are part of Olympics/Asian Games/other major international 
competitions shall be considered for the Games under this component. In addition 
to this other sports/indigenous sports shall also be considered based on their 
popularity.  
5.1.3. The competitions will be organised in collaboration with concerned National 
Sports Federations (NSFs), Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), 
Association of Indian Universities (AIU), and other relevant stakeholders. 
5.1.4. The framework for the strengthening of the domestic competition structure is as 
follows: 
a. Flagship Games – Competitive National level events focused on funnelling 
India’s best talent to international standards. 
b. Thematic Games –  Competitions designed to promote regional/coastal 
community and culturally significant games, ensuring inclusivity and 
diversity in sport. 
c. Leagues –School/University/Regional/Sports-Specific Leagues to provide 
regular competitive exposure, early talent identification, aligning education 
and sports, encouraging sports specific leagues and alignment with annual 
sports calendars. 
5.1.5. The framework will also include ASMITA Leagues to expand women’s 
participation, Sports for Peace and Development in disturbed and border areas to 
engage youth constructively, promotion of rural, indigenous and tribal games to 
facilitate main -streaming of the concerned sports, and dedicated support for 
 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 30 
 
persons with disabilities to strengthen para-sports participation and performance. 
 
5.2. Implementation Mechanism 
5.2.1. Flagship Games 
a. Flagship (National Level) Competitions: These events shall be conducted 
periodically, including Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India University 
Games, and other such national events are envisioned to reflect India’s 
preparation for future Olympic (Summer & Winter) and Paralympic Games. 
The flagship Games shall be conducted periodically depending upon the 
requirements. Further, accessibility shall be considered for aforesaid 
competitions, especially for Para Sports.  
b. The games shall be conducted in association with a State/UT Government for 
which an MoU will be signed indicating the broad areas of responsibilities. 
The concerned State/UT Government will take care of Host city 
infrastructure, Sports infrastructure, Sports Equipment, Venue Readiness, 
Branding, etc. wherever required. Other stakeholders will be involved in the 
smooth conduct of the games. 
c. Organising Committee (OC) will be constituted at national level for direction 
and guidance for the successful conduct of the Games. The composition of 
the committee shall include the Hon’ble Minister for Youth Affairs and 
Sports as the Chairperson, with the Hon’ble Chief Minister and Sports 
Minister of the respective State/UT Government. Representatives of SAI, 
relevant NSFs, and Host State/UT , etc. will be included. The Chairperson 
may co-opt any additional members as deemed necessary for the event being 
organised. 
d. Additionally, an Executive Committee (EC) will be constituted for the 
smooth conduct of the Games and will supervise and monitor different 
activities of the Games chaired by the Secretary (Sports), MYAS and Co -
Chaired by Chief Secretary/Administrator of State/ UT Government and 
members from representative MY AS/SAI, State/UT Government and 
National Sports Federation. The Chairperson may co -opt any additional 
members as deemed necessary for the event being organised. 
 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 31 
 
e. Further, the Host State/UT shall also constitute additional committees as per 
requirement for the conduct of the Games, including an Organising 
Committee and an Executive Committee with ex -athlete, sports 
administrators, and educational institutions representation encouraged. 
f. A separate Games Technical Conduct Committee (GTCC) may be constituted 
for all relevant competitions/events with members of Sports Authority of 
India, a subject expert of the concerned sports discipline, representative of 
the NSF, host State/UT, CBSE/SGFI/AIU/PCI/IOA, other relevant 
stakeholders. GTCC shall have the mandate for the technical conduct of the 
relevant competitions/events. 
5.2.2. Thematic Games: 
a. These competitions include Khelo India Beach Games, Khelo India Water 
Sports, Khelo India Tribal Games, Khelo India Swadeshi Games, Khelo India 
North-East Games, and the Khelo India Martial Arts Games and other such 
events. 
b. The competitions shall follow similar organisation mechanisms as flagship 
events, including the signing of MoUs with host State/UT, formation of 
OC/EC, GTCC and others.  
5.2.3. Khelo India Leagues 
a. The inclusion of structured league systems will be implemented to support 
the conduct of regular competition exposure for athletes and supplement the 
efforts of the flagship/thematic events. A circuit of leagues including School 
League, University League , Regional/Sport-specific league and others will 
be developed aligning with academic calendars, strengthening 
school/university competition ecosystem and suit custom requirements of 
sports respectively.  
b. Regional/Sports specific leagues may be conducted through SAI Regional 
Centres/State sports departments/NSF/various Khelo India Training 
Facilities to ensure custom needs of each sport are met.  
c. Leagues will be organized in partnership with the NSFs/ Sports Bodies and 
Central/State education bodies, progressing from local and district levels to 
state/national stages. 
 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 32 
 
5.2.4. Achieving Sports Milestones by Inspiring women Through Action (ASMITA) 
a. While all the components of the Khelo India Scheme are gender neutral and 
afford opportunities to women for participating in sporting activities, 
dedicated competition mechanisms have been created to support women 
participation.  
b. Through ASMITA, emphasis will be laid on such sports disciplines where 
there is less participation of women so that a greater number of women will 
participate in such sports disciplines. Preference may be given to sports 
disciplines which are part of Olympic/Asian Games an d other major 
international competitions. 
5.2.5. Sports for Peace and Development 
a. The Khelo India Scheme envisages the usage of sports for the promotion of 
peace and development in terrorism and extremism-affected areas as well as 
other disturbed areas and areas along the international land border to promote 
confidence-building among the local populace and bringing the youth into 
the mainstream and engaging them in healthy and constructive activities. 
b. The sporting activities/sports competitions  in eligible States/UTs/districts 
shall be organised in collaboration with various organisations under Ministry 
of Home Affairs and Ministry of Defence.  
5.2.6. Promotion of Rural and Indigenous/Tribal Games (PRITG) 
a. The PRITG sub -component aims to promote rural, indigenous and tribal 
games/sports by raising awareness, engaging young people, and encouraging 
wider participation to support their mainstreaming.  
b. The list of games/sports to be included under this sub-component shall be 
issued from time to time.  
c. Proposals shall be submitted by States/UTs, NSFs, and other suitable entities. 
5.2.7. Promotion of Sports among Persons with Disabilities 
a. Competitions for Persons with Disabilities (Para, Deaf  and others) shall be 
organised in collaboration with the concerned NSF wherever feasible. 
b. Proposals shall be submitted by States/UTs, NSFs, and other suitable entities.

5.3. Operational Framework 
5.3.1. A structured competition calendar will ensure regular access to quality events, 
promote integration with NSF rankings and selection systems, encourage youth 
engagement through internships, volunteerism and spectatorship, and adopt 
sustainable and inclusive event practices. Events will be hosted across States and 
UTs to maximize the use of existing sports infrastructure and enhance the capacity 
of host regions to organise major sporting events.  
5.3.2. Efforts may be made to align the Khelo India events calend ar with the Annual 
Calendar for Training and Competition of concerned NSFs. 
5.3.3. This component shall be executed by associating with specialized organisations 
like NSFs, Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), Association of Indian 
Universities (AIU)/University Sports Board, State/UT Governments and other 
stakeholders as will be required. A system may be developed for managing results, 
records and others which shall be synchronized with all stakeholders. All 
Stakeholders may maintain the data for all level competitions i.e. grassroot, pre -
district, district, zonal, state, national and others. 
5.3.4. Integration of technology for Timing, Scoring  and Results (TSR), and Games 
Management System (GMS), as well as other areas shall be explored and 
implemented with all the concerned stakeholders across all levels (grassroot, pre-
district, district, zonal, state, national and others). Integration with other platforms 
of Khel Setu will be ensured. 
5.3.5. All events under the Khelo India Scheme may follow a standardized structure with 
participation from stakeholders at district, zonal, state, and national levels. The 
competition framework will serve as a key pathway for talent identification and 
progression into Khelo India Training Facilities. 
5.3.6. Suitable Khelo India branding guidelines to be followed across all events, as 
applicable. 
5.3.7. A suitable mechanism may  be devised to ensure doping awareness workshops 
before competitions for athletes and coaches keeping in view the inclusion of the 
spirit of fair play and integrity in sports.  
5.3.8. Necessary anti -doping awareness and testing to be taken up across various 
competitions.

5.3.9. Mechanisms for convergence with other components of the scheme may be 
explored to map sports talent with regional and demographic characteristics.

competition structures.

a. The competitions organised by NSF/AIU/CBSE may act as avenues for the 
identification of athletes  across sports disciplines for participation in Khelo

decision/approval as detailed in Chapter 12 – Approval and Monitoring 
Mechanism - of the Operational Guidelines 
 
5.5. Funding and Monitoring Mechanism 
5.5.1. An appropriate budget will be earmarked for the conduct of all 
competitions/leagues/events under this component. 
5.5.2. Wherever feasible, convergence or co-funding be undertaken with other schemes 
of the Ministry, other Ministries or Departments of the Government of India, 
States/UTs, institutions, MPLADS, MLALADS, CSR initiatives, public or private 
entities, PPP models, a nd corporate sponsorships. Such support shall be clearly 
disclosed, approvals to be taken where required, and used to supplement Scheme 
assistance without duplication of funding for the same activity or expenditure. 
5.5.3. The competent authority may  establish an administrative mechanism to 
periodically monitor the progress and preparation for each event, learnings, 
quality of conduct and outcome of the event.  
  
 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 35 
 
6. Talent Identification & Development 
6.1. Introduction 
6.1.1. The Talent Identification and Development (TID) component targets to strengthen 
the process through harmonized protocols, coordinated implementation, and 
advanced sports science and digital platforms. The initiative ensures that talent is 
identified early and channelled into structured training programs. This approach 
creates a seamless pipeline from grassroots to elite performance, reflecting global 
best practices where nations significantly improved medal tallies through early 
talent identification coupled with world-class infrastructure and scientific training 
and monitoring. 
6.1.2. The number of athletes supported under this component shall be significantly 
increased with emphasis on priority sports.  
6.1.3. The TID component will drive convergence among State/UTs, NSFs, institutions, 
and private entities for coordinated talent development. 
 
6.2. Implementation Mechanism 
6.2.1. To cater to the convergence requirement and to bring more athletes under a 
structured monitoring and nurturing system, the TID framework shall operate 
through a tiered athlete development structure comprising four stages: 
a. Foundation Level: 
i. Foundation level includes beginners and young children starting their 
sports journey 
ii. Training is undertaken to introduce basic skills, physical fitness, and 
interest in sports 
iii. Foundation level will be catered through active collaboration with the 
Ministry of Education for integrating school ecosystem with sports.  
b. Grassroots Level: 
i. Grassroots level includes Athletes who show potential at the school or 
community level. This potential talent may be identified through schools, 
school leagues or other interventions by the department.  
ii. For the identified talent, t raining to be undertaken to provide early- stage 
coaching. 
 
 
  
KHELO INDIA SCHEME (2026-27 TO 2030-31): OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES 36 
 
iii. Training centres include Khelo India Utkrishta Vidyalayas, Khelo India 
Feeder Schools and Khelo India Centres. 
c. Intermediate Level: 
i. Intermediate Stage athletes are categorised as Emerging Khelo India 
Athletes (E -KIA) or Khelo India Athletes (KIA) based on the age -
appropriate protocols and benchmarks.  
ii. Training is undertaken in the facilities of Sports Authority of India 
Training Centres (STC), SAI National Centre of Excellence (NCoE ), 
Khelo India Accredited Academy (KIAA), Khelo India Centre of 
Excellence (Including Universities), Youth Sports Companies (in 
collaboration with Armed Forces) and other suitable acade

4. PRE-QUALIFICATION CRITERIA  
The intending Bidder should fulfill the following minimum pre-qualifying criteria: 
 
1. Turnover: Average Annual Financial Turnover on construction works during the last 3 years, ending 31st March of the previous financial year i.e. 2025-26, should be at least 100% of the estimated cost. Applicant has to attach the Balance Sheet along with profit & loss statement duly certified by Chartered Accountant for last five years. 
1.1. Note: In case the Balance sheet for FY 2025-26 has not been audited yet then Audited balance sheet for FY 2022-23, FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 shall be considered for evaluation. Applicant has to attached Balance sheet along with profit and Loss Statement duly certified by Chartered Accountant 
 
2. Experience: Bidder should have the experience of completion of similar works during last 7 years ending last day of month previous to the one in which tenders are invited should be either of the following: 
Three similar completed works each costing not less than the amount equal to 40% of the estimated cost. Certificate should be attached. 
Or 
Two similar completed works each costing not less than the amount equal to 50% of the estimated cost. Certificate should be attached. Or 
One similar completed work costing not less than the amount equal to 80% of the estimated cost. Certificate should be attached.  Similar works mean: “Similar works” shall mean “Interior works comprising Interior Works, Civil works, Internal Electrical Works, Sanitary works, Air Conditioning / VRV/VRF/HVAC, Fire Fighting works, Low Voltage Works- Fire alarm, PA system, CCTV works, Access control , Audio video and video conferencing system , IT works in a single contract, at Government Organizations/Semi Government Organization of Central or State Government; or by Public Sector Undertakings/ Autonomous Bodies or private offices large multinational companies.”  Note:- Work executed with Central/State Govt./Semi-Govt. Organisations/ Authorities, PSUs, Govt. of India under takings shall only be considered to qualify above eligibility. Certificates from the private Individuals/Organizations shall not be considered.

3. Profitability: The applicant should be a profit-making firm and have not incurred losses for more than two years out of last five years ending 31st March, 2026 duly certified by Chartered Accountant. 
 
3.1. Note: In case the Balance sheet for FY 2025-26 has not been audited yet then Audited balance sheet for last 5 years ending FY 2024-25 shall be considered for evaluation. Applicant has to attached Balance sheet along with profit and Loss Statement duly certified by Chartered Accountant 
 
4. Solvency Certificate: Tenderer must have solvency for an amount equal to 40% of the estimated cost duly certified by the bank and to be uploaded while submitting the tender on website. Solvency Certificate up to 6 (six) months before the last date of submission of tender will be acceptable. 
 
5. EPF Registration: Preferably agency should have EPF registration, in case EPF registration is not there, the agency should obtain EPF registration on allotment of work. In case of failure, SAI will deduct EPF & deposit as per EPF norms. 
 
6. Goods & Service Tax (GST) Registration: Bidder must have valid Goods & Services Tax Registration. Also, the GST filing should be submitted up to 31 March 2025 from 1st April 2022. 
 
7. Joint Venture: Joint Ventures are not permitted. 
 
8. Bid Capacity: Agencies who meet the minimum qualification criteria will be qualified only if their available bid capacity is more than the total bid value. The available bid capacity will be calculated as under: 
Assessed available bid capacity = (A x N x 2) - B 
N = Number of years rounded up to first decimal prescribed for completion of the subject contract. 
A = Maximum value of works executed in anyone year during last five years (up dated to the price level of current financial year with percentage stated in the PQ document). 
B = Value at current price level of existing commitments and ongoing works to be completed in the next 'N' years. 
Note: 
8.1. The Applicant shall furnish statements showing the value of existing commitments and on-going works as well as the stipulated period of completion remaining for each of the works preferably countersigned by the Nodal Officer or his nominee- in-charge in the format available in documents. 
8.2. Financial Turnover of previous years shall be given weightage of 5% (simple rate) per annum based on rupee value to bring them to current financial year price level. 
8.3. The value of executed works shall be brought to current costing level by enhancing the actual value of work at simple rate of 7% per annum calculated from the date of completion to last date of receipt of applications for tenders.

0.1   BRIEF SCOPE OF WORK 
1.1 OBJECTIVE OF THE PROJECT 
 
The proposed project comprises the comprehensive renovation and modernization of the new office 
space for the National Sports Federations (NSFs) at I.G. Stadium Complex, New Delhi.  
The scope includes civil, interior, furniture, electrical, HVAC, fire safety, and audio-visual works to 
develop a functional, aesthetically pleasing and technologically equipped office environment 
comprising office cabins, workstations, conference hall, circulation areas, and associated support 
spaces. 
• Execution of anti-termite treatment using approved chemical emulsion in the renovated areas to 
provide long-term protection against termite infestation.  
• Repair and restoration of damaged civil components, including granite flooring and window sills, 
vitrified tile flooring, cement plaster, ceilings and concrete members using approved repair materials, 
including SBR polymer-modified mortar, wherever required.  
• Providing and fixing Aluminium Composite Panel (ACP) cladding, complete with structural steel 
supporting framework, for the exterior façade of the conference hall and other approved locations.  
• Construction and modification of office cabins and internal spaces by providing flush door shutters 
with second-class teak wood frames, 66 mm thick gypsum dry-wall partitions and associated 
finishing work as per the approved layout.  
• Repairing and upgrading roof and ceiling systems, including pre-coated galvanized iron (GI) profile 
sheet roofing over the conference hall, repair of gypsum board and GI metal ceilings and providing 
new gypsum false ceilings in office areas.  
• Providing and installing interior finishes, including WPC louvers, 12 mm thick HDHMR wall 
paneling, decorative wallpaper, fabric-faced acoustic wall cladding, decorative baffle ceiling in the 
conference hall and zebra blinds for windows to enhance aesthetics, functionality, and acoustic 
performance.  
• Carrying out complete painting and finishing works, including surface preparation, primer, putty, 
and application of approved paint systems on walls, ceilings, woodwork, and steelwork.  
• Providing, laying, testing, and commissioning of complete electrical installations, including 
concealed electrical wiring, power outlets, modular switches, workstation power points, and 
data/internet outlets for all office spaces.  
• Providing and installing electrical distribution infrastructure, including Distribution Boards (DBs), LT 
cables, earthing system, cable trays, and associated accessories for safe and reliable power 
distribution.  
• Providing and fixing LED light fixtures, Occupancy sensor, wall fan, for office areas, cabins, 
conference hall, and common spaces.  
• Repair, testing, and commissioning of fire detection alarm systems, sprinklers, and all associated 
accessories, all required as per site requirement.

• Providing, installing, testing, and commissioning of new HVAC provision comprising VRV/VRF air-
conditioning units with refrigerant piping, ducting, diffusers, grilles, and accessories, along with split 
air-conditioning units wherever required.  
• Providing and installing a complete Audio-Visual (AV) system for the conference hall, including 
display units, display screen, speakers, microphones, and associated accessories for seamless 
conferencing and presentations.  
• Supply, installation, testing, and commissioning of all furniture, electrical, HVAC, AV, and allied
